final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition with CHF 10 billion government loss protection, SNB liquidity bridge, and a Sunday 6 AM public statement naming the buyer. However, funding stress climbed to 95 by meeting end, breaching the critical threshold before the planned announcement, leaving the rescue's viability in doubt.
minority_objections: CS CEO objected to Saturday depositor briefings as signaling weakness
AT1 representative demanded legally binding guarantee language locked tonight, not Sunday morning
Wealth client warned that 36-hour information vacuum (Friday night to Sunday 6 AM) would trigger liquidity flight regardless of Sunday statement
key_conflicts: Timing of public disclosure: Friday 11 PM liquidity statement vs. waiting until Sunday 6 AM for full announcement

uncertainty_notes: Meeting terminated with funding stress at 95, already past the 92 threshold the room identified as critical. The Sunday 6 AM statement strategy was locked but its viability was in doubt given the accelerating stress. The Saturday 4 PM conditional guarantee activation was discussed but never formally approved or documented. Whether the UBS LOI would actually be signed by 10 PM Friday remained unconfirmed at meeting end. The exact legal language binding the CHF 10B cap was promised but not yet distributed to all parties.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: SNB's CHF 5B liquidity bridge was deployed but explicitly framed as insufficient without loss protection and buyer commitment; drove the CHF 10B government guarantee as binding constraint
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the singular rescue path; UBS CEO's conditional LOI signature by 10 PM Friday was the meeting's central decision point and timeline driver
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 10B Federal Council loss guarantee was the non-negotiable foundation of the deal; Federal Council's absolute cap shaped all other terms and became a binding red line
marker_evidence.client_flight: Funding stress climbing from 74 to 95 drove every major decision: Friday 11 PM statement timing, Saturday 4 PM guarantee activation threshold, Sunday 6 AM announcement deadline
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 absorbing losses beyond CHF 10B cap was explicitly locked as the loss allocation mechanism; AT1 rep demanded legally binding guarantee language tonight to protect creditors from Saturday triage
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Discussed as AT1 vs. taxpayer loss allocation and cherry-pick clause enforcement, but did not force a concession or change the CHF 10B cap structure—acknowledged and set aside
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: Not mentioned in any substantive way
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Friday 10 PM LOI deadline, Saturday 4 PM conditional activation threshold, Sunday 6 AM statement deadline—all driven by need to announce before Monday market open; time pressure climbed from 58 to 77
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Mentioned as background motivation (market panic if no buyer visible Monday) but did not itself force a specific decision—the funding stress metric and weekend timeline drove concrete choices
